editorial.headline: Private Religious Higher Education, Open Nationally and Clearer in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Private religious higher education is nationally open to PMA, while Bali’s risk-based treatment keeps it outside the provincial moratorium.
editorial.body:
KBLI 85404 frames private religious higher education: provision at diploma, bachelor’s, master’s and doctoral levels, alongside equivalent academic, professional and vocational programmes. Its defining thread is not religious study in isolation. The stated scope combines general knowledge and religious values, while also providing specialised courses centred on religious disciplines. It is therefore an education activity with room for both wide academic study and focused religious scholarship.

The record names private universities, institutes, higher schools and *ma’had aly* as its institutional forms. Its examples include Islamic universities, theology colleges and seminary colleges. These indicate the range of private higher-education settings contemplated by the activity, without narrowing it to a single religious tradition or academic format. It is open at every recorded business scale: micro, small, medium and large. That broad scale access does not change the essential character of the activity, which remains higher education integrating general scholarship with religious values.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is direct. The PMA status is open, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. A foreign investor may therefore hold the full foreign stake permitted nationally for this activity. The record identifies Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 as its PMA source. The central point for founders is straightforward: religious higher education in this private institutional form is not presented here as a nationally closed PMA activity.

Bali requires an exact reading rather than a dramatic one. Its recorded status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK; the reason classifies the activity as medium-high/high risk and says it is not blocked by the moratorium, subject to verification by address. Bali’s permanent island-wide PMA moratorium applies to all low and medium-low risk KBLI activities. As recorded, this activity sits outside that blocked set. It should not be described as barred to PMA registration in Bali today, but address-level verification remains part of the locally stated picture.
editorial.pullQuote: As recorded, this activity sits outside Bali’s blocked set.
